items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We had met Oscar Pettiford a few times and he came to see us at our hotel... Of course I saw many of my musician friends and buddies... Oscar Pettiford opened a club... and I was there on opening night with Lily of course.

ctx.x: A few nights later, after my meeting with Kirby, I was in bar in Broadway where many of the cats hung out and met Jimmy Wright, whom I had worked with in a dancing school many moons ago. Jimmy played tenor and after a few drinks and some chit-chat about days gone by, Jimmy started telling me about how well he was doing and bragging about his Lincoln car. Finally I got around to telling him that I was in the market for a tenor man and told him what it was for. As we had worked together, I figured it would be a…

We had met Oscar Pettiford a few times and he came to see us at our hotel, bringing my wife big bottles of perfume. He decided to spend the last night with us. That last night on that side of the pond was the most. It started at the Metropole, then we went to Jimmy Ryan's as we wanted to dig the Wilbur de Paris band that was loaded with fellows I had known a long time and had also worked with at certain times. There was Sydney de Paris playing trumpet and bass tuba, which I didn't know that he played. I've seen…

When Ryan's place closed, Oscar offered to take us up town to Minton's Playhouse. We had no idea of what group was playing there but that didn't matter because Minton's always had good musicians playing there. And one of my old bosses, Teddy Hill was the manager and I'm almost certain that he was at least part owner of the place. I had not seen Teddy since 1946 when we met on a street in Manila in the Philippines and we were happy to see each other again.
